profile.bio: I build infrastructure that can be rebuilt from a single commit: Go services with append-only state, NixOS fleets with their own certificate authority, and data pipelines that turn operational noise into a decision. Most of that work has been in energy — telemetry, valuation and risk across renewable portfolios worth more than $100M. The rest is vulnerability data, where CISA's KEV catalogue is the raw material.

focus.title: Reproducible fleets
focus.body: NixOS and flakes across servers, workstations and a cloud endpoint. One commit describes the machine; a switch is the deployment.

focus.title: Go services with bounded work
focus.body: Server-rendered binaries and append-only event logs. No frontend build, no framework, small enough to audit in an afternoon.

focus.title: Vulnerability data that ends in action
focus.body: KEV as a time series and as work clusters: what is exploited now, and which patch order removes the most risk per hour spent.

work.title: Multi-host NixOS fleet
work.description: One flake for a fleet of NixOS hosts: NAS, workstations, a cloud endpoint and a remote builder, an SSH certificate authority with rotation, encrypted secrets, and a taskfile as the only interface. Every host is commissioned by registering one line.
highlights: One flake describes ten hosts: a NAS, workstations, a cloud endpoint and a remote builder.
An SSH certificate authority with rotation, and SOPS-encrypted secrets per host and user.
A taskfile is the only operator interface, so no host carries its own runbook.
The same module gate runs locally and in CI, which is what makes a passing switch evidence.

work.title: bountystash: deterministic work engine
work.description: A single Go binary that turns a request into an immutable, content-addressed specification: append-only events, keyboard-first terminal UI, curl-friendly endpoints, zero frontend dependencies.
highlights: An append-only event log, so every state is a replay of recorded facts.
One Go binary serves HTML, JSON and a keyboard-first TUI; there is no frontend build.
Specifications are content-addressed, so the same request yields the same document.
curl-friendly endpoints, which is what makes it usable in the middle of an incident.

work.title: fibtransponder
work.description: A Fibonacci-radix streaming state machine for tokenization experiments: bounded per-step work over a bitstream, adjacency width as a locality selector, Zobrist seed tables, and a corpus benchmark that falsified the seed-only detector.
highlights: A Fibonacci-radix streaming state machine over a bitstream, with bounded work per step.
Adjacency width works as a locality selector instead of a global lookup table.
Zobrist seed tables keep the state transitions cheap enough to stream.
A corpus benchmark falsified the seed-only detector, so the claim got smaller instead of louder.

work.title: Energy telemetry and valuation
work.description: Quantitative steering of a solar portfolio above $100M: yield and valuation models that survived bank audits, mobile field data capture, and counterparty risk that institutional lenders accepted.
highlights: Yield and valuation models that survived bank audits on a portfolio above $100M.
Mobile field capture feeding the same pipeline as the meteorological data.
Counterparty risk reported in the form institutional lenders accepted.
Telemetry reconciliation that turned missing sensor data into a known error budget.

lab.title: The KEV lab
lab.body: Two public tools make CISA's Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalogue legible. kev-time plots exploitation over time, so a trend is visible before a report exists. kelly-svg groups entries into clusters a team can work through, so the patch plan follows from data instead of instinct. Both are static SVG and plain HTML, built to be read on a phone during an incident. A third page puts the same data in the shape of a programme: a sample queue of exploited entries grouped by effort, at concept.bountystash.com.
